1	# Spec: Study Policy, Query, and CLI Surface (Item 12)
2	
3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Owner:** Reid W
5	**Created:** 2026-07-12
6	**Complexity:** MEDIUM
7	**Branch:** constraint-exec-epic
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Problem
12	
13	Items 10 and 11 built the study machine but left no way for a person to drive it. The
14	evaluator (Item 10) turns typed inputs into immutable `ModelEvidence`; the store, runner, and
15	strategies (Item 11) run a list or grid of candidates crash-safely and commit one case per
16	candidate. All of that is reachable today only from Python test code: a study is a
17	hand-assembled `StudyDefinition`, the policy is a stub (`DispositionPolicy`) whose only real
18	job is to exercise the `assessment_failed` path, and reading results back means writing raw
19	SQL against the store and hand-decoding the non-finite sentinel in staged artifacts.
20	
21	Three gaps remain, and they are the whole point of the study layer for a user:
22	
23	- **Policy is a stub.** `DispositionPolicy` maps a headline to a disposition string and fails
24	  assessment only for an injected set of candidate IDs (`study/policy.py:31`). The concept's
25	  policy — the user-selected *interpretation* of evidence, which decides whether a verdict
26	  means reject the point, penalize it, keep it for a boundary plot, or feed it back to a
27	  strategy — does not exist yet.
28	- **There is no query surface.** Results live across three places (the `cases` row's inputs
29	  and state, the content-addressed evidence artifact, the catalog), and nothing joins them.
30	  A user cannot ask "which points violated constraint X" or "show me the boundary" without
31	  raw SQL and manual sentinel decoding.
32	- **There is no CLI.** The repo has no console entry point at all. The concept's define → run
33	  → interrupt → resume → inspect story has no surface a user can invoke.
34	
35	This item builds those three surfaces on top of the certified code, changing nothing in the
36	evaluator or the crash-safe store/runner contracts.
37	
38	## Success Criteria
39	
40	- [ ] **Grid study runs end-to-end from the CLI:** define → run → interrupt → resume → query,
41	  over the sealed fixture package, with the resumed store's ordered cases identical to an
42	  uninterrupted run (byte-identical case order, states, and committed evidence digests).
43	- [ ] **The full policy protocol interprets evidence into the four dispositions** (reject,
44	  penalize, keep-for-boundary, feed-strategy) and **never mutates stored evidence**; a
45	  policy-*rejected* point is a `completed` case that still carries its outputs and violation
46	  verdicts (a boundary-plot point), distinct from an `assessment_failed` case.
47	- [ ] **Policy failure yields `assessment_failed` with evidence intact** — reachable through a
48	  real objective/policy extraction failure, not only the test-only injected reject set.
49	- [ ] **The query distinguishes both axes:** the three case states
50	  (`completed | execution_failed | assessment_failed`) and the three verdict classes
51	  (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate`), and can filter cases by parameter, output,
52	  constraint ID, status, and assessment.
53	- [ ] **The query read path decodes the non-finite sentinel:** a NaN or infinite output or
54	  observed operand in a staged artifact reads back as a real non-finite float (or an explicit
55	  non-finite marker), never as the raw `{"__nonfinite__": …}` dict.
56	- [ ] **Resume refuses a changed fingerprint with a new-lineage message** instead of mixing
57	  datasets, and the query can join static source detail (source form, membership kind,
58	  polarity, owner) through the catalog keyed by `constraint_id`.
59	- [ ] teax suite green; Ruff clean.
60	
61	## Known Requirements
62	
63	Grading: behaviors forced by the certified Item 10/11 code or the fixture are `[HARD]`;
64	intents carried from the owner-ratified concept/epic are `[INHERITED]` with source cited;
65	`[INFERRED]` marks a reading not stated verbatim. See `capture-fidelity.md`.
66	
67	### Policy — interpretation over immutable evidence
68	
69	- **[INHERITED]** **The policy is the user-selected interpretation of one evaluation's
70	  evidence, producing one of four dispositions: reject, penalize, keep-for-boundary,
71	  feed-strategy.** Compute/judge/decide are separate: the policy is the only place a verdict
72	  becomes a decision about the exploration. (concept Design Principle 1, "Study Layer", Vocabulary
73	  `study policy`; epic Item 12 §1.)
74	- **[HARD]** **Assessment never mutates stored evidence.** `ModelEvidence` is a frozen
75	  `StrictBaseModel` (`evaluation/evidence.py:45`); the runner serializes evidence to the
76	  artifact independently of the assessment (`study/runner.py:_assess_and_commit`). The full
77	  policy receives evidence read-only and returns a separate assessment record; the artifact
78	  bytes are unchanged by it. (concept Required Invariant "policy assessment never mutates
79	  stored evidence".)
80	- **[HARD]** **`assessment_failed` preserves the real evidence.** When the policy raises
81	  `AssessmentFailed`, the runner still stages the true `evidence_json` and commits an
82	  `assessment_failed` case beside it (`study/runner.py:133–143`) — never a stub. The full
83	  protocol keeps this contract. (concept Edge Cases "Objective extraction or policy fails:
84	  evidence is preserved in an assessment-failed record, never relabeled model failure".)
85	- **[INFERRED]** **`assessment_failed` becomes reachable through a genuine extraction/policy
86	  error, not only the injected `reject_candidate_ids` set.** That set is a documented test
87	  affordance the deterministic fixture needs (`study/conftest.py`); the production protocol
88	  fails when, for example, an objective it must extract is absent or non-numeric — matching
89	  the concept's "objective extraction or policy fails". The injected-set affordance may remain
90	  for tests but is not the only path.
91	- **[INFERRED]** **A policy *disposition* is orthogonal to the case *state*.** "Reject" is a
92	  policy verdict recorded in the assessment of a `completed` case, not the `assessment_failed`
93	  case state (which means the policy itself broke). This distinction must be explicit so a
94	  boundary-plot query can find policy-rejected points among `completed` cases.
95	- **[INHERITED]** **"Penalize" carries a raw objective/penalty value, never a normalized
96	  one.** Penalties and objectives are extracted as modeled quantities; inventing a normalized
97	  penalty scale is a non-goal. (concept Non-Goals "Invent … normalized penalties".)
98	- **[INHERITED]** **The study selects objectives by output ID and response roles; the policy
99	  cannot redefine a predicate.** `StudyDefinition` was specified to carry objectives and
100	  response roles (Item 11 `spec.md#studydefinition`), though the dataclass carries only
101	  `budget`/`retention` as uninterpreted `Any` today (`study/definition.py:44`). Item 12 gives
102	  objectives/response roles their interpretation for the policy to consume. (concept "Study
103	  Layer"; epic Item 12 §1.)
104	
105	### Query — results joined through the catalog
106	
107	- **[INHERITED]** **Results query by parameter, output, constraint ID, status, and
108	  assessment.** (concept "Inspect and Resume".)
109	- **[HARD]** **The query reads three stores and joins them:** the `cases` row
110	  (`inputs_json` = parameters, `state`, `assessment_json`), the content-addressed evidence
111	  artifact reached via `evidence_digest` (selected `outputs`, per-constraint `responses`, the
112	  opaque `report`), and the catalog. (`study/store.py` schema; `study/evidence_io.py`
113	  payload shape.)
114	- **[HARD]** **The read path decodes the non-finite sentinel.** `encode_evidence` tags every
115	  non-finite float as `{"__nonfinite__": "nan"|"inf"|"-inf"}` recursively across responses,
116	  outputs, provenance, and report (`study/evidence_io.py:20`). The query's decode is the exact
117	  inverse: a tagged value reads back as the corresponding real float (or an explicit
118	  non-finite marker), and a nested one-key `{"__nonfinite__": …}` never leaks to the caller as
119	  a dict. This is the read half of Item 11's D3 write path. (brief Notes; `study/evidence_io.py`.)
120	- **[INHERITED]** **Static source detail joins through the catalog, keyed by `constraint_id`.**
121	  A per-constraint verdict in a case (e.g. `toy_plant__demo_plant__affordable → violated`)
122	  joins to the catalog's concrete entry and its source record to surface source form,
123	  membership kind, polarity, owner, and display predicate — so a query can group failures by
124	  modeled constraint while naming the failing instance. (concept "Catalog, Evaluation, and
125	  Report"; fixture `contracts/constraint_catalog.json`.)
126	- **[HARD]** **The catalog available to this item is the sealed fixture's
127	  `constraint_catalog.json`** — `source_records` (keyed by `usage_name`) and
128	  `concrete_entries` (keyed by `constraint_id`, referencing `source_usage`). Item 9's
129	  `ModelContract` is not yet built; the query consumes the fixture's catalog shape and the seam
130	  to `ModelContract` is named, not bridged. (brief Notes; epic Item 9 lands later in
131	  sysml-codegen.)
132	- **[INHERITED]** **The query distinguishes the three case states and three verdict classes.**
133	  States (`completed | execution_failed | assessment_failed`) come from the `cases.state`
134	  column; verdict classes (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate`) come from the evidence
135	  `responses`/report. Both axes are filterable and reported. (epic Item 12 success criteria;
136	  `study/store.py`, `evaluation/evidence.py:16`.)
137	- **[INHERITED]** **Tracking-key correlation shows fingerprint boundaries — names correlate,
138	  never equate.** A `tracking_key` names a logical constraint across model versions; correlated
139	  results whose evidence spans different executable fingerprints must be shown *as* spanning a
140	  boundary, never merged into one constraint. (concept "Concrete Lowering" `tracking_key`
141	  paragraph; epic Item 12 §2.)
142	- **[INFERRED]** **For this item, tracking-key correlation is scoped to surfacing the boundary,
143	  not spanning stores.** One `StudyStore` binds exactly one `executable_fingerprint`
144	  (`study/compatibility.py`), and the fixture catalog carries no `tracking_key`. The realizable
145	  deliverable is: every query result carries its `executable_fingerprint`, and the correlation
146	  contract marks the boundary — so a consumer that later correlates across fingerprints cannot
147	  silently equate them. True cross-fingerprint correlation needs `tracking_key` in the catalog
148	  (Item 5/9) plus multi-store data; that mechanism is deferred (see Open Questions). *(Surfaced
149	  per capture-fidelity Law 4 rather than silently narrowed.)*
150	
151	### CLI — create / run / resume / inspect
152	
153	- **[INHERITED]** **The CLI provides create, run, resume, and inspect contracts** over one
154	  study, and a grid study runs end-to-end through them over the sealed fixture package. (epic
155	  Item 12 §3 + success criterion; concept "Run a Study", "Inspect and Resume".)
156	- **[HARD]** **Resume refuses a changed fingerprint and starts a new lineage.** Reopening a
157	  store whose bound compatibility differs raises `IncompatibleStore`
158	  (`study/store.py:_check_compatibility`); the CLI must catch it and render a new-lineage
159	  message rather than a stack trace. The compatibility binding is the eight fields in
160	  `study/compatibility.py` (executable, model-contract, study-definition fingerprints; schema
161	  versions; strategy identity and order-sensitive config). (concept Required Invariant "Resume
162	  joins on study lineage … never on constraint IDs alone"; epic Item 12 §3.)
163	- **[HARD]** **Resume requires the study definition to be persistent and reconstructable.** The
164	  store binds only the *compatibility fingerprints*, not the live `StudyDefinition` (its
165	  strategy object, `entry_model` type, validator, and policy) — and the runner needs a live
166	  definition to propose and evaluate (`study/runner.py:45`). So resume must rebuild the same
167	  definition from a re-readable source and hand it to the runner; the store then checks
168	  compatibility. (`study/definition.py`, `study/store.py`.)
169	- **[HARD]** **Resume is idempotent by candidate.** The runner skips any candidate whose case
170	  already exists (`store.has_case`, `study/runner.py:62`), so a resumed run reproduces the
171	  uninterrupted run's ordered cases exactly — the property the end-to-end test asserts. (Item 11
172	  Required Invariant; `study/runner.py`.)
173	- **[INHERITED]** **A rejected point retains its outputs and violations for boundary plots.**
174	  A policy-rejected point is a `completed` case with full evidence staged; the CLI/query
175	  exposes those outputs and violation verdicts. (concept "Run a Study"; epic Item 12 §3.)
176	
177	### Cross-cutting
178	
179	- **[HARD]** **Model, assessment, and persistence failures stay phase-distinct end to end.**
180	  The CLI/query must not collapse an `execution_failed` case, an `assessment_failed` case, and
181	  a feasible-but-`indeterminate` verdict into one bucket — the runner already keeps them
182	  distinct (`study/runner.py`); the surfaces preserve that. (concept "Run a Study"; Required
183	  Invariant "Proposal records and the three case states never merge".)
184	
185	## Implementation Prerequisites (not API requirements)
186	
187	- **Provision teax's own venv as the first implementation step**, as Items 10 and 11 did —
188	  teax's own environment is broken for real-simkit runs and the spikes borrowed the
189	  fusion-tea/agentic-mbse venv with a `PYTHONPATH` graft. This is a sequencing prerequisite,
190	  not a contract of the policy/query/CLI surface. (epic Risks "teax environment provisioning".)
191	
192	## Non-Goals
193	
194	- **Visualization and plotting.** The query retains the data a boundary plot needs; it draws
195	  nothing. (epic Item 12 Out of Scope.)
196	- **Optimizer configuration and adaptive strategies.** Only prepared lists and grids exist;
197	  `observe()` is inert. The policy may *classify* a feed-strategy disposition, but wiring that
198	  feedback into an adaptive strategy is deferred with S7. (epic Item 12 Out of Scope; concept
199	  "Study Layer"; `study/strategy.py`.)
200	- **Contract authoring or sealing.** `ModelContract`/`PackageContract` derivation is Item 9;
201	  this item *consumes* the fixture's catalog and package.
202	- **True cross-fingerprint (multi-store) tracking-key correlation.** Deferred; needs
203	  `tracking_key` in the catalog and multi-store data (see Query requirements and Open
204	  Questions).
205	- **Changing the evaluator or the store/runner crash-safety contracts.** Item 12 is additive
206	  over certified code.
207	
208	## Open Questions / Deferred to design
209	
210	- **CLI study-definition source — the shape of "create" (owner decision at design).** `create`
211	  must produce a persistent, re-readable definition that `resume` can reconstruct (a `[HARD]`
212	  requirement above). Two mechanisms, both meeting it:
213	  - *(A) Declarative study-config file* (e.g. YAML/JSON) naming the sealed package, grid
214	    variables/domains by parameter ID, the strategy, a policy (by name/config), and
215	    budget/retention. The CLI resolves `entry_model` from the loaded package and synthesizes
216	    the grid proposal-validator. Most CLI-native; most build.
217	  - *(B) Python-entrypoint reference* — `create` points at an importable module that returns a
218	    `StudyDefinition`; the CLI owns the run/resume/inspect/query lifecycle around it. Thinner;
219	    "define" stays in Python.
220	  *Recommendation:* a lean (A) sufficient for the grid case (package ref + variables/domains +
221	  a built-in disposition/objective policy + synthesized validator), with the policy selectable
222	  from a small registry. This is what makes the end-to-end grid test real inside the 1-day
223	  budget. Reserve the final call for the owner at design, as Item 10 reserved its entry-source
224	  shape.
225	- **Where objectives and response roles live** — extend the `StudyDefinition` dataclass
226	  (currently `budget`/`retention` as `Any`) with typed objective/response-role fields, versus
227	  carrying them in the policy's own config. Interacts with the study-definition fingerprint.
228	- **The objective-extraction failure rule** — exactly which conditions (missing output ID,
229	  non-numeric objective, unresolved response role) raise `AssessmentFailed`. Design should
230	  state the rule rather than leave it implicit.
231	- **Query result shape and how much reads eagerly** — whether the query returns typed records
232	  or dicts, and whether it decodes/join-loads every evidence artifact eagerly or lazily.
233	  Mechanism; defer.
234	- **Tracking-key correlation scope confirmation** — whether design commits only to surfacing
235	  `executable_fingerprint` per result (the inferred single-store scope above) or reaches for a
236	  cross-store correlation contract now. Flagged so it is decided deliberately, not by default.
237	- **CLI packaging** — the console-script entry name and whether it ships in `teax-simkit`'s
238	  `pyproject.toml`. Mechanism; defer.
239	- **Budget and retention interpretation** — how `budget` bounds a run and how `retention`
240	  interacts with the store's GC. Carried uninterpreted by Item 11; design decides the rule.
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Related Artifacts
245	
246	- **Epic:** `.project/reference/epic_constraint_execution.md` — Item 12 (canonical:
247	  sysml-codegen `.project/backlog/epic_constraint_execution.md`).
248	- **Required Reading (from the epic):**
249	  - `.project/reference/constraint-execution-concept.md` — "Study Layer"; "How It Works" (Run a
250	    Study; Inspect and Resume); Vocabulary; Design Principle 1; Required Invariants (Study
251	    Execution); Edge Cases.
252	- **Depends on (certified on this branch):**
253	  - Item 11 — `.project/active/study-store-runner/` (store DDL, runner, strategies,
254	    `DispositionPolicy` stub, sentinel encoding, compatibility binding, lease).
255	  - Item 10 — `.project/active/model-evaluator/` (`ModelEvidence`, failure taxonomy,
256	    projection vocabulary).
257	- **Code specced against:** `simkit/study/` (policy, store, runner, definition, strategy,
258	  evidence_io, compatibility, bridge, identity, failures); `simkit/evaluation/` (evidence,
259	  projection, failure, evaluator); fixture
260	  `simkit/tests/evaluation/fixtures/sealed_package/package_live/contracts/constraint_catalog.json`.
261	- **Design:** `.project/active/study-policy-cli/design.md` (to be created).
262	
263	---
264	
265	**Next Steps:** After approval, proceed to `/_my_spec_review` (fresh session), then
266	`/_my_design`. Design must resolve the reserved CLI study-definition shape with the owner.

  `study policy`; epic Item 12 §1.)
- **[HARD]** **Assessment never mutates stored evidence.** `ModelEvidence` is a frozen
  `StrictBaseModel` (`evaluation/evidence.py:45`); the runner serializes evidence to the
  artifact independently of the assessment (`study/runner.py:_assess_and_commit`). The full
  policy receives evidence read-only and returns a separate assessment record; the artifact
  bytes are unchanged by it. (concept Required Invariant "policy assessment never mutates
  stored evidence".)
- **[HARD]** **`assessment_failed` preserves the real evidence.** When the policy raises
  `AssessmentFailed`, the runner still stages the true `evidence_json` and commits an
  `assessment_failed` case beside it (`study/runner.py:133–143`) — never a stub. The full
  protocol keeps this contract. (concept Edge Cases "Objective extraction or policy fails:
  evidence is preserved in an assessment-failed record, never relabeled model failure".)
- **[INFERRED]** **`assessment_failed` becomes reachable through a genuine extraction/policy
  error, not only the injected `reject_candidate_ids` set.** That set is a documented test
  affordance the deterministic fixture needs (`study/conftest.py`); the production protocol
  fails when, for example, an objective it must extract is absent or non-numeric — matching
  the concept's "objective extraction or policy fails". The injected-set affordance may remain
  for tests but is not the only path.
- **[INFERRED]** **A policy *disposition* is orthogonal to the case *state*.** "Reject" is a
  policy verdict recorded in the assessment of a `completed` case, not the `assessment_failed`
  case state (which means the policy itself broke). This distinction must be explicit so a
  boundary-plot query can find policy-rejected points among `completed` cases.
- **[INHERITED]** **"Penalize" carries a raw objective/penalty value, never a normalized
  one.** Penalties and objectives are extracted as modeled quantities; inventing a normalized
  penalty scale is a non-goal. (concept Non-Goals "Invent … normalized penalties".)
- **[INHERITED]** **The study selects objectives by output ID and response roles; the policy
  cannot redefine a predicate.** `StudyDefinition` was specified to carry objectives and
  response roles (Item 11 `spec.md#studydefinition`), though the dataclass carries only
  `budget`/`retention` as uninterpreted `Any` today (`study/definition.py:44`). Item 12 gives
  objectives/response roles their interpretation for the policy to consume. (concept "Study
  Layer"; epic Item 12 §1.)

### Query — results joined through the catalog

- **[INHERITED]** **Results query by parameter, output, constraint ID, status, and
  assessment.** (concept "Inspect and Resume".)
- **[HARD]** **The query reads three stores and joins them:** the `cases` row
  (`inputs_json` = parameters, `state`, `assessment_json`), the content-addressed evidence
  artifact reached via `evidence_digest` (selected `outputs`, per-constraint `responses`, the
  opaque `report`), and the catalog. (`study/store.py` schema; `study/evidence_io.py`
  payload shape.)
- **[HARD]** **The read path decodes the non-finite sentinel.** `encode_evidence` tags every
  non-finite float as `{"__nonfinite__": "nan"|"inf"|"-inf"}` recursively across responses,
  outputs, provenance, and report (`study/evidence_io.py:20`). The query's decode is the exact
  inverse: a tagged value reads back as the corresponding real float (or an explicit
  non-finite marker), and a nested one-key `{"__nonfinite__": …}` never leaks to the caller as
  a dict. This is the read half of Item 11's D3 write path. (brief Notes; `study/evidence_io.py`.)
- **[INHERITED]** **Static source detail joins through the catalog, keyed by `constraint_id`.**
  A per-constraint verdict in a case (e.g. `toy_plant__demo_plant__affordable → violated`)
  joins to the catalog's concrete entry and its source record to surface source form,
  membership kind, polarity, owner, and display predicate — so a query can group failures by
  modeled constraint while naming the failing instance. (concept "Catalog, Evaluation, and
  Report"; fixture `contracts/constraint_catalog.json`.)
- **[HARD]** **The catalog available to this item is the sealed fixture's
  `constraint_catalog.json`** — `source_records` (keyed by `usage_name`) and
  `concrete_entries` (keyed by `constraint_id`, referencing `source_usage`). Item 9's
  `ModelContract` is not yet built; the query consumes the fixture's catalog shape and the seam
  to `ModelContract` is named, not bridged. (brief Notes; epic Item 9 lands later in
  sysml-codegen.)
- **[INHERITED]** **The query distinguishes the three case states and three verdict classes.**
  States (`completed | execution_failed | assessment_failed`) come from the `cases.state`
  column; verdict classes (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate`) come from the evidence
  `responses`/report. Both axes are filterable and reported. (epic Item 12 success criteria;
  `study/store.py`, `evaluation/evidence.py:16`.)
- **[INHERITED]** **Tracking-key correlation shows fingerprint boundaries — names correlate,
  never equate.** A `tracking_key` names a logical constraint across model versions; correlated
  results whose evidence spans different executable fingerprints must be shown *as* spanning a
  boundary, never merged into one constraint. (concept "Concrete Lowering" `tracking_key`
  paragraph; epic Item 12 §2.)
- **[INFERRED]** **For this item, tracking-key correlation is scoped to surfacing the boundary,
  not spanning stores.** One `StudyStore` binds exactly one `executable_fingerprint`
  (`study/compatibility.py`), and the fixture catalog carries no `tracking_key`. The realizable
  deliverable is: every query result carries its `executable_fingerprint`, and the correlation
  contract marks the boundary — so a consumer that later correlates across fingerprints cannot
  silently equate them. True cross-fingerprint correlation needs `tracking_key` in the catalog
  (Item 5/9) plus multi-store data; that mechanism is deferred (see Open Questions). *(Surfaced
  per capture-fidelity Law 4 rather than silently narrowed.)*

### CLI — create / run / resume / inspect

- **[INHERITED]** **The CLI provides create, run, resume, and inspect contracts** over one
  study, and a grid study runs end-to-end through them over the sealed fixture package. (epic
  Item 12 §3 + success criterion; concept "Run a Study", "Inspect and Resume".)
- **[HARD]** **Resume refuses a changed fingerprint and starts a new lineage.** Reopening a
  store whose bound compatibility differs raises `IncompatibleStore`
  (`study/store.py:_check_compatibility`); the CLI must catch it and render a new-lineage
  message rather than a stack trace. The compatibility binding is the eight fields in
  `study/compatibility.py` (executable, model-contract, study-definition fingerprints; schema
  versions; strategy identity and order-sensitive config). (concept Required Invariant "Resume
  joins on study lineage … never on constraint IDs alone"; epic Item 12 §3.)
- **[HARD]** **Resume requires the study definition to be persistent and reconstructable.** The
  store binds only the *compatibility fingerprints*, not the live `StudyDefinition` (its
  strategy object, `entry_model` type, validator, and policy) — and the runner needs a live
  definition to propose and evaluate (`study/runner.py:45`). So resume must rebuild the same
  definition from a re-readable source and hand it to the runner; the store then checks
  compatibility. (`study/definition.py`, `study/store.py`.)
- **[HARD]** **Resume is idempotent by candidate.** The runner skips any candidate whose case
  already exists (`store.has_case`, `study/runner.py:62`), so a resumed run reproduces the
  uninterrupted run's ordered cases exactly — the property the end-to-end test asserts. (Item 11
  Required Invariant; `study/runner.py`.)
- **[INHERITED]** **A rejected point retains its outputs and violations for boundary plots.**
  A policy-rejected point is a `completed` case with full evidence staged; the CLI/query
  exposes those outputs and violation verdicts. (concept "Run a Study"; epic Item 12 §3.)

### Cross-cutting

- **[HARD]** **Model, assessment, and persistence failures stay phase-distinct end to end.**
  The CLI/query must not collapse an `execution_failed` case, an `assessment_failed` case, and
  a feasible-but-`indeterminate` verdict into one bucket — the runner already keeps them
  distinct (`study/runner.py`); the surfaces preserve that. (concept "Run a Study"; Required
  Invariant "Proposal records and the three case states never merge".)

## Implementation Prerequisites (not API requirements)

- **Provision teax's own venv as the first implementation step**, as Items 10 and 11 did —
  teax's own environment is broken for real-simkit runs and the spikes borrowed the
  fusion-tea/agentic-mbse venv with a `PYTHONPATH` graft. This is a sequencing prerequisite,
  not a contract of the policy/query/CLI surface. (epic Risks "teax environment provisioning".)

## Non-Goals

- **Visualization and plotting.** The query retains the data a boundary plot needs; it draws
  nothing. (epic Item 12 Out of Scope.)
- **Optimizer configuration and adaptive strategies.** Only prepared lists and grids exist;
  `observe()` is inert. The policy may *classify* a feed-strategy disposition, but wiring that
  feedback into an adaptive strategy is deferred with S7. (epic Item 12 Out of Scope; concept
  "Study Layer"; `study/strategy.py`.)
- **Contract authoring or sealing.** `ModelContract`/`PackageContract` derivation is Item 9;
  this item *consumes* the fixture's catalog and package.
- **True cross-fingerprint (multi-store) tracking-key correlation.** Deferred; needs
  `tracking_key` in the catalog and multi-store data (see Query requirements and Open
  Questions).
- **Changing the evaluator or the store/runner crash-safety contracts.** Item 12 is additive
  over certified code.

## Open Questions / Deferred to design

- **CLI study-definition source — the shape of "create" (owner decision at design).** `create`
  must produce a persistent, re-readable definition that `resume` can reconstruct (a `[HARD]`
  requirement above). Two mechanisms, both meeting it:
  - *(A) Declarative study-config file* (e.g. YAML/JSON) naming the sealed package, grid
    variables/domains by parameter ID, the strategy, a policy (by name/config), and
    budget/retention. The CLI resolves `entry_model` from the loaded package and synthesizes
    the grid proposal-validator. Most CLI-native; most build.
  - *(B) Python-entrypoint reference* — `create` points at an importable module that returns a
    `StudyDefinition`; the CLI owns the run/resume/inspect/query lifecycle around it. Thinner;
    "define" stays in Python.
  *Recommendation:* a lean (A) sufficient for the grid case (package ref + variables/domains +
  a built-in disposition/objective policy + synthesized validator), with the policy selectable
  from a small registry. This is what makes the end-to-end grid test real inside the 1-day
  budget. Reserve the final call for the owner at design, as Item 10 reserved its entry-source
  shape.
- **Where objectives and response roles live** — extend the `StudyDefinition` dataclass
  (currently `budget`/`retention` as `Any`) with typed objective/response-role fields, versus
  carrying them in the policy's own config. Interacts with the study-definition fingerprint.
- **The objective-extraction failure rule** — exactly which conditions (missing output ID,
  non-numeric objective, unresolved response role) raise `AssessmentFailed`. Design should
  state the rule rather than leave it implicit.
- **Query result shape and how much reads eagerly** — whether the query returns typed records
  or dicts, and whether it decodes/join-loads every evidence artifact eagerly or lazily.
  Mechanism; defer.
- **Tracking-key correlation scope confirmation** — whether design commits only to surfacing
  `executable_fingerprint` per result (the inferred single-store scope above) or reaches for a
  cross-store correlation contract now. Flagged so it is decided deliberately, not by default.
- **CLI packaging** — the console-script entry name and whether it ships in `teax-simkit`'s
  `pyproject.toml`. Mechanism; defer.
- **Budget and retention interpretation** — how `budget` bounds a run and how `retention`
  interacts with the store's GC. Carried uninterpreted by Item 11; design decides the rule.

---

## Related Artifacts

- **Epic:** `.project/reference/epic_constraint_execution.md` — Item 12 (canonical:
  sysml-codegen `.project/backlog/epic_constraint_execution.md`).
- **Required Reading (from the epic):**
  - `.project/reference/constraint-execution-concept.md` — "Study Layer"; "How It Works" (Run a
    Study; Inspect and Resume); Vocabulary; Design Principle 1; Required Invariants (Study
    Execution); Edge Cases.
- **Depends on (certified on this branch):**
  - Item 11 — `.project/active/study-store-runner/` (store DDL, runner, strategies,
    `DispositionPolicy` stub, sentinel encoding, compatibility binding, lease).
  - Item 10 — `.project/active/model-evaluator/` (`ModelEvidence`, failure taxonomy,
    projection vocabulary).
- **Code specced against:** `simkit/study/` (policy, store, runner, definition, strategy,
  evidence_io, compatibility, bridge, identity, failures); `simkit/evaluation/` (evidence,
  projection, failure, evaluator); fixture
  `simkit/tests/evaluation/fixtures/sealed_package/package_live/contracts/constraint_catalog.json`.
- **Design:** `.project/active/study-policy-cli/design.md` (to be created).

---

**Next Steps:** After approval, proceed to `/_my_spec_review` (fresh session), then
`/_my_design`. Design must resolve the reserved CLI study-definition shape with the owner.

1	# Design: Study Policy, Query, and CLI Surface (Item 12)
2	
3	**Status:** Draft
4	**Owner:** Reid W
5	**Created:** 2026-07-12
6	**Branch:** constraint-exec-epic
7	**Base commit:** 3a30b47
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Overview
12	
13	Three thin user surfaces over the certified Item 10/11 machinery: a full **policy** that
14	interprets immutable evidence into one of four dispositions, a **query** that joins the case
15	row + evidence artifact + catalog and decodes the non-finite sentinel, and a **CLI** that
16	drives create → run → interrupt → resume → inspect over a declarative study-config file.
17	
18	## Related Artifacts
19	
20	- **Spec:** `.project/active/study-policy-cli/spec.md` (the `[HARD]` items below are fixed there).
21	- **Design brief:** `.project/active/study-policy-cli/briefs/` (orchestrator decisions D-CLI, D-track).
22	- **Epic:** `.project/reference/epic_constraint_execution.md` — Item 12.
23	- **Required Reading:** `.project/reference/constraint-execution-concept.md` — "Study Layer",
24	  "Run a Study", "Inspect and Resume", Vocabulary, Design Principle 1.
25	- **Consumed as-is (certified):** `simkit/study/` (store, runner, strategy, compatibility,
26	  evidence_io, definition, bridge, identity, crash), `simkit/evaluation/` (evaluator, evidence,
27	  projection, package_load).
28	
29	## Research Findings
30	
31	The certified code already fixes almost every seam this item plugs into. Key facts:
32	
33	- **The runner never sees the definition source.** `StudyRunner.run` drives
34	  `definition.strategy.propose`, `definition.validate_proposal`, `definition.policy.assess`, and
35	  `bridge.build` (`study/runner.py:45–66`). It calls `policy.assess(evidence, candidate_id=…)`
36	  with no other context (`runner.py:132`). So a richer policy must close over its config at
37	  construction — the assess signature and the runner call site stay untouched.
38	- **Evidence is frozen and encoded independently of assessment.** `_assess_and_commit` encodes
39	  evidence to the artifact *before* calling the policy, and stages the true evidence even on
40	  `AssessmentFailed` (`runner.py:130–143`). Non-mutation and evidence-preservation are already
41	  structural; the full policy inherits them for free.
42	- **The store already distinguishes both axes.** `cases.state` holds
43	  `completed|execution_failed|assessment_failed`; the evidence `responses`/`report` hold the
44	  `satisfied|violated|indeterminate|not_assessed` verdicts (`store.py:62–71`,
45	  `evaluation/evidence.py:16`, `constraint_types.py`). The query reads, never re-derives them.
46	- **Compatibility is an eight-field frozen binding checked on every reopen** (`compatibility.py`;
47	  `store.py:_check_compatibility` raises `IncompatibleStore`). Resume correctness is *already*
48	  enforced by the store; the CLI only needs to rebuild the same `StudyDefinition` and render the
49	  refusal instead of a stack trace.
50	- **The evaluator hands back everything the CLI needs to assemble a definition:**
51	  `evaluator.package`, `evaluator.fingerprint`, `EVIDENCE_SCHEMA_VERSION`, and the entry-model
52	  type (`evaluator.py:77–107`; `package_load.py`). `conftest.build_definition` is the exact
53	  template (`tests/study/conftest.py:177`).
54	- **The sentinel is a pure recursive tag** (`evidence_io.py:_tag_nonfinite`) with a reserved
55	  one-key `{"__nonfinite__": …}` shape. Its inverse is mechanical and belongs beside it.
56	- **The catalog fixture** (`…/package_live/contracts/constraint_catalog.json`) has
57	  `concrete_entries` keyed by `constraint_id` (→ `source_usage`, `owner_instance`,
58	  `membership_kind`, `is_negated`) and `source_records` keyed by `usage_name` (→ `source_form`,
59	  `owner_qn`, `definition_qn`, `predicate_ir`). The join is `constraint_id → source_usage →
60	  source_record`.
61	- **Item 11 already ships a deterministic crash seam.** `CrashController` `os._exit(137)`s at a
62	  named `(phase, candidate_id)` (`study/crash.py`); `_study_child.py` wires it from a `--crash-at`
63	  argument. The CLI reuses this exact mechanism for the interrupt test — no timing races.
64	
65	## Core Concept
66	
67	This item is **plumbing, not machinery**. The certified runner/store already produce and persist
68	everything correctly; nobody can drive them and nobody can read the results back. So we add three
69	adapters and change no contract:
70	
71	1. **Policy = interpretation, closed over its config.** A named policy from a small built-in
72	   registry reads immutable evidence (outputs, per-constraint verdicts, headline) and returns a
73	   separate assessment record naming one of four dispositions — reject, penalize,
74	   keep-for-boundary, feed-strategy. It fails to `assessment_failed` only when it genuinely cannot
75	   extract a required objective or response role. It never touches the artifact bytes; the runner
76	   already staged them.
77	
78	2. **Query = a read-only join with the sentinel decoded.** One `StudyQuery` reads the `cases`
79	   rows, loads and decodes each referenced evidence artifact once, and joins per-constraint
80	   verdicts to the catalog by `constraint_id`. It surfaces both axes (three case states, three
81	   verdict classes), carries each result's `executable_fingerprint` as the correlation boundary
82	   marker, and filters by parameter, output, constraint, status, state, and disposition.
83	
84	3. **CLI = a lifecycle over a declarative config file.** A study-config file (YAML) *is* the
85	   persistent, re-readable definition. `create` builds a `StudyDefinition` from it and binds the
86	   store; `run`/`resume` rebuild the same definition and drive the runner (the store's
87	   compatibility check enforces they match); `inspect` renders the query. The config's semantic
88	   digest is the `study_definition_fingerprint`, so an edited config is a new lineage by
89	   construction.
90	
91	The key insight: **the config file replaces the hand-assembled `StudyDefinition`, and the store's
92	existing compatibility binding — not new CLI logic — is what makes resume safe.** Everything else
93	is a faithful adapter over certified code.
94	
95	## Key Bets
96	
97	- **B1. The declarative config carries enough to reconstruct a byte-identical `StudyDefinition`
98	  across processes.** Package ref + entry channel/model name + ordered grid + fixed fields + policy
99	  block + budget/retention fully determine the definition; nothing definition-shaping lives only in
100	  Python. *If false → resume rebuilds a subtly different definition, the fingerprint diverges, and
101	  either a valid resume is refused or (worse) identity silently shifts.*
102	- **B2. A policy can be a genuine interpretation while reading evidence strictly read-only.** The
103	  four dispositions are computable from `outputs` + `responses` + configured objectives alone,
104	  with no need to re-run or mutate anything. *If false → the policy needs to recompute or amend
105	  evidence, breaking the non-mutation invariant and the whole "compute/judge/decide are separate"
106	  premise.*
107	- **B3. The fixture catalog shape is a sufficient stand-in for the future `ModelContract`.** Its
108	  `concrete_entries`/`source_records` carry every static field the query must surface (source form,
109	  membership kind, polarity, owner, display predicate). *If false → the query cannot name failing
110	  instances and the catalog-join success criterion is unmet until Item 9.*
111	
112	## Key Decisions
113	
114	- **D1. Config format = YAML, with a Pydantic config schema.** *Rejected: JSON (the repo already
115	  drives pipelines from YAML; a hand-edited study file wants comments and readability); an ad-hoc
116	  dict loaded without validation (loses fail-fast on a malformed study).* 
117	- **D2. `study_definition_fingerprint` = digest of the config's *semantic* subset, excluding
118	  filesystem locations.** Digest `study_id`, entry channel/model name, ordered grid, fixed fields,
119	  policy block, budget, retention — not `package.dir`, spec path, or store path. Package identity is
120	  separately bound via `executable_fingerprint` (the seal). *Rejected: digesting the whole config
121	  file (a moved package dir or renamed store would spuriously start a new lineage); a hand-authored
122	  fingerprint field (drifts from content).*
123	- **D3. The policy closes over its config; the assess signature and runner call site are
124	  unchanged.** The CLI builds the concrete policy from the definition's `objectives`/`response_roles`
125	  and hands it in. *Rejected: extending `Policy.assess` to receive objective context (edits the
126	  certified runner call at `runner.py:132` for no behavioral gain).*
127	- **D4. Objectives and response roles are typed fields on `StudyDefinition` (additive, defaulting
128	  empty).** They populate from the config and feed the policy factory; the config digest (D2) puts
129	  them in the fingerprint. *Rejected: carrying them only inside policy config (the `[INHERITED]`
130	  requirement is that `StudyDefinition` carries them; empty defaults keep `conftest` compiling).*
131	- **D5. `decode_evidence` lives next to `encode_evidence` in `study/evidence_io.py`; the query
132	  imports it.** One inverse, one home. *Rejected: a decode in `query.py` (duplicates the sentinel
133	  contract across two files — the exact drift the encode module's INV-H docstring warns against).*
134	- **D6. Query is Python-first (`StudyQuery` returning typed records); the CLI `inspect` renders
135	  it.** *Rejected: CLI-only string output (the join is the testable unit and a future notebook/plot
136	  consumer needs the records, per concept "Inspect and Resume").*
137	- **D7. Query decodes eagerly, memoized by digest.** Each referenced artifact is read+decoded once,
138	  cached by `evidence_digest`. *Rejected: lazy per-field loading (a real abstraction cost for
139	  fixture-scale grids that fit in memory); re-reading per case (duplicate reads for replicate
140	  digests).*
141	- **D8. Interrupt = the certified `CrashController` wired through a hidden, test-only `--crash-at`
142	  argument.** Mirrors `_study_child.py`. *Rejected: `SIGKILL` on the subprocess (nondeterministic
143	  crash point makes "some cases committed, one not" flaky).*
144	- **D9. Budget/retention get a thin, optional interpretation.** `budget` (int) caps candidates via
145	  an additive `BoundedStrategy` wrapper; `retention: gc_after` calls the existing `store.gc()` after
146	  the lease releases (default `keep`). *Rejected: leaving them inert (spec asks design to state the
147	  rule); wiring budget into the runner (certified). Both are low-stakes and not load-bearing for the
148	  acceptance test — see Handoff.*
149	
150	## Architecture
151	
152	```
153	study-config.yaml ──► StudyConfig (Pydantic)          [study/config.py]
154	        │                    │
155	        │        ┌───────────┼──────────────┬───────────────────┐
156	        ▼        ▼           ▼              ▼                   ▼
157	  ProvisionalPackageLoader  GridStrategy  synthesized-validator  POLICY_REGISTRY[name]
158	        │                                                        (objectives, roles)
159	        ▼                                                        │
160	  PreparedEvaluator ──► entry_model, fingerprint, schema ver     ▼
161	        └──────────────────────────► StudyDefinition ◄───── ObjectivePolicy
162	                                          │  (+objectives, response_roles: D4)
163	                                          ▼
164	   create ─► StudyStore.create_or_open(compat)         [certified]
165	   run/resume ─► open → acquire_lease → StudyRunner.run(crash) → release  [certified]
166	                                          │
167	                                          ▼  reads
168	   inspect ─► StudyQuery(store, catalog) ─┼─► cases rows (state, inputs, assessment)
169	                                          ├─► evidence artifact via digest → decode_evidence
170	                                          └─► catalog join by constraint_id
171	                                              → CaseView[] (both axes, fingerprint, catalog detail)
172	```
173	
174	**Data flow, create:** load config → load+seal package → build `PreparedEvaluator` → resolve
175	`entry_model` = `getattr(evaluator.package, config.entry_model)` → build `GridStrategy` from the
176	ordered variable list → synthesize the proposal-validator (coerce numeric, merge fixed fields) →
177	build the policy from the registry → assemble `StudyDefinition` (all fingerprints; D2 semantic
178	digest) → `StudyStore.create_or_open` binds compatibility → copy the config beside the store as a
179	record.
180	
181	**Data flow, resume:** rebuild the definition from the *same* config → `create_or_open` on the
182	existing store → `_check_compatibility` raises `IncompatibleStore` on any changed fingerprint → CLI
183	catches it and prints the new-lineage message. Otherwise acquire lease and run; the runner's
184	`has_case` skip makes it idempotent by candidate.
185	
186	**Failure routing** is unchanged — the runner already keeps `execution_failed` /
187	`assessment_failed` / feasible-but-`indeterminate` distinct; the surfaces only read them.
188	
189	## Required Invariants
190	
191	- **INV-1. Assessment never mutates evidence.** The policy receives frozen `ModelEvidence` and
192	  returns a new dict; the artifact bytes are produced by `encode_evidence` before assess runs. (Test:
193	  artifact digest identical whether the policy rejects, penalizes, or fails.)
194	- **INV-2. Disposition ⊥ case state.** A policy-*rejected* point is a `completed` case whose
195	  `assessment_json.disposition == "reject"`; an `assessment_failed` case means the policy itself
196	  broke. The query filters the two independently.
197	- **INV-3. `decode_evidence` is the exact inverse of `encode_evidence`.** For any evidence,
198	  `decode(encode(e))` restores every non-finite float and leaves no `{"__nonfinite__": …}` dict in
199	  the caller-visible payload. (Test: round-trip over nan/inf/-inf in responses, outputs, report.)
200	- **INV-4. Resume reproduces the uninterrupted ordered cases exactly.** After a mid-run crash,
201	  `resume` yields byte-identical case order, states, and `evidence_digest`s vs. an uninterrupted run
202	  over the same config. (The acceptance test.)
203	- **INV-5. Every query result carries its `executable_fingerprint`.** Read from evidence provenance
204	  (and equal to the store's bound fingerprint); the query never merges across fingerprints.
205	
206	## Component Overview
207	
208	- **`study/config.py`** — `StudyConfig` Pydantic schema (package ref, entry channel/model, ordered
209	  grid, fixed fields, policy block, budget, retention), a YAML loader, and `semantic_fingerprint()`
210	  (D2). Synthesizes the grid proposal-validator.
211	- **`study/policy.py`** (extend) — add `ObjectivePolicy` implementing the four-disposition
212	  interpretation and the objective-extraction failure rule (below). Keep `DispositionPolicy` (tests
213	  use it). Add `POLICY_REGISTRY: dict[str, PolicyFactory]` mapping name → factory taking
214	  `(objectives, response_roles, config)`.
215	- **`study/definition.py`** (extend) — add `objectives: tuple[ObjectiveSpec, …] = ()` and
216	  `response_roles: Mapping[str, str] = {}` (D4).
217	- **`study/evidence_io.py`** (extend) — add `decode_evidence` (D5).
218	- **`study/query.py`** — `StudyQuery` over a store + catalog; `CaseView` and `CatalogView` typed
219	  records; filters. Uses `decode_evidence`; joins the catalog by `constraint_id`.
220	- **`study/cli.py`** — argparse `create|run|resume|inspect`; wires the evaluator/store/runner/query;
221	  catches `IncompatibleStore`; hidden `--crash-at` (D8). `main()` is the console entry point.
222	- **`study/bounded_strategy.py`** (optional, D9) — `BoundedStrategy(inner, max_candidates)`, an
223	  additive strategy wrapper for `budget`.
224	- **`pyproject.toml`** — `[project.scripts] teax-study = "simkit.study.cli:main"`.
225	
226	### The policy: dispositions and the failure rule
227	
228	`ObjectivePolicy.assess(evidence, *, candidate_id)` (signature unchanged):
229	
230	1. **Extract objectives.** For each configured objective (an `output` ID + a `role` such as
231	   `minimize`/`maximize`/`penalty`), read `evidence.outputs[output]`. Extract response-role verdicts
232	   by resolving each configured role to a `constraint_id` in `evidence.responses`.
233	2. **Objective-extraction failure rule** → raise `AssessmentFailed` (spec asked design to state it):
234	   a configured objective `output` ID is **absent** from `evidence.outputs`, **or** a configured
235	   response role names a constraint **absent** from `evidence.responses`. A well-formed
236	   `indeterminate`/`violated`/`not_assessed` verdict, and a non-finite objective value, are **not**
237	   failures — they are interpreted, not rejected. This is genuinely reachable (configure an objective
238	   on an output the evidence lacks), distinct from Item 11's injected `reject_candidate_ids`.
239	3. **Map to a disposition** from the headline verdict and objective thresholds:
240	   `violated → reject`; `indeterminate | not_assessed → keep-for-boundary`;
241	   `satisfied` within threshold `→ feed-strategy`; `satisfied` beyond a configured penalty threshold
242	   `→ penalize`.
243	4. **Return the assessment record** (a plain dict, stored in `cases.assessment_json`):
244	   `{"disposition", "headline", "objectives": {id: raw_value}, "penalty": raw_or_null}`. Penalize
245	   carries the **raw** objective/penalty value — never a normalized scale (spec `[INHERITED]`).
246	
247	### Config schema (illustrative, ~schema not code)
248	
249	```yaml
250	study_id: toy-grid-demo
251	package: { dir: <package_live>, name: wi014_s4, spec: pipelines/pipeline.yaml }
252	entry_channel: toy_plant_params
253	entry_model: ToyPlantParams            # attribute on the loaded package module
254	grid:                                  # ordered [param_id, domain] pairs (D8 order = identity)
255	  - [toy_plant__Toy_Plant__plant_budget, [1000.0, 3000.0, 6000.0]]
256	fixed: { toy_plant__Toy_Plant__plant_length: 4.0, ...unit_cost: 250.0, ...width: 3.0 }
257	policy:
258	  name: objective/v1
259	  objectives: [ { output: cost, role: minimize } ]
260	  response_roles: {}
261	budget: null                           # optional int cap (D9)
262	retention: keep                        # keep | gc_after (D9)
263	```
264	
265	## Non-Goals
266	
267	- Visualization/plotting; optimizer configuration and adaptive-strategy feedback (`feed-strategy`
268	  is classified, not wired).
269	- Contract authoring/sealing; the query consumes the fixture catalog and the `ModelContract` seam is
270	  named, not bridged.
271	- True cross-fingerprint (multi-store) tracking-key correlation; the query only surfaces each
272	  result's `executable_fingerprint` boundary (orchestrator D-track; note for Item 14 docs).
273	- Any change to the evaluator or the store/runner crash-safety contracts. All changes are additive.
274	- A Python-entrypoint `create` shape (orchestrator picked lean Option A; can be added later without
275	  breaking A).
276	
277	## Implementation Notes
278	
279	- **Provision teax's own venv first** (spec prerequisite; Items 10/11 did the same). The end-to-end
280	  test runs the real evaluator over the sealed package.
281	- **`entry_model` resolution:** use `getattr(evaluator.package, config.entry_model)`, not the
282	  fixture-specific `evaluator.ToyPlantParams` attribute — keep the CLI package-agnostic.
283	- **Synthesized validator** must mirror `conftest.validate_proposal`: numeric-and-not-bool coercion
284	  to `float`, then merge `fixed` fields into the canonical map. Non-finite is valid (it evaluates to
285	  `indeterminate`), malformed/missing/wrong-type returns `None`.
286	- **Grid + fixed:** the strategy proposes only variable fields; the validator injects `fixed`.
287	  Fields in neither fall to the entry model's own defaults (bridge behavior, `bridge.py:18`).
288	- **Provisional `model_contract_fingerprint`:** derive from a digest of the catalog file bytes and
289	  label it a provisional stand-in until Item 9 (`conftest` uses a literal; a catalog digest is
290	  more honest and still stable). Do not invent a `ModelContract`.
291	- **New-lineage message** must be actionable: name the differing binding and tell the user a new
292	  store path (or reverted config) is needed — never a bare `IncompatibleStore` traceback.
293	- **`decode_evidence`** must reject nothing the encoder produced and must leave genuine one-key
294	  dicts unmolested only if they are the sentinel shape; mirror `_tag_nonfinite`'s recursion exactly.
295	
296	## Potential Risks
297	
298	- **Fingerprint drift on resume (B1).** If any definition-shaping input is omitted from the
299	  semantic digest (D2), resume mis-binds. *Mitigation:* the acceptance test (INV-4) is a
300	  create→run→crash→resume round-trip that fails loudly on any drift; unit-test the digest over a
301	  config edited in each field.
302	- **Genuine `assessment_failed` not exercised by the happy grid.** `cost` is present for every real
303	  grid point, so the natural grid never fails extraction. *Mitigation:* a dedicated policy test
304	  configures an objective on a missing output ID to hit the rule genuinely; the end-to-end test
305	  need not itself fail assessment (spec lists the two as separate criteria).
306	- **Config path portability.** Absolute `package.dir` in the config is environment-specific.
307	  *Mitigation:* excluded from the fingerprint (D2); resume still works if the package moved, as long
308	  as its sealed bytes (→ `executable_fingerprint`) are unchanged.
309	- **Budget wrapper changes strategy identity.** A `BoundedStrategy` alters `strategy_config`.
310	  *Mitigation:* correct by design (a bounded study is a distinct lineage); its `config_fingerprint`
311	  includes both the inner config and the bound. Budget is optional (D9).
312	
313	## Integration Strategy
314	
315	Purely additive over certified code. The CLI is a new console entry point in `teax-simkit`; the
316	policy/definition/evidence_io extensions default to the current behavior so all Item 10/11 tests keep
317	passing. Nothing in `evaluation/` or the store/runner crash-safety path changes. The catalog read is
318	the named seam to Item 9's `ModelContract`.
319	
320	## Validation Approach
321	
322	- **Acceptance (INV-4), `test_cli_end_to_end.py`:** write a grid config; `create`; `run --crash-at
323	  before_commit:<mid candidate>` in a subprocess (exits 137); `resume`; then a reference
324	  uninterrupted `create`+`run` over the same config. Assert the resumed store's `ordered_cases()`
325	  equals the reference's — case order, states, and `evidence_digest`s byte-identical.
326	- **Policy unit tests:** all four dispositions produced from crafted evidence; disposition ⊥ state
327	  (INV-2); genuine `AssessmentFailed` on a missing objective ID and on an unresolved response role;
328	  raw (un-normalized) penalty value; evidence-digest identical across dispositions (INV-1).
329	- **Query unit tests:** three states × three verdict classes surfaced and filterable; sentinel
330	  round-trip (INV-3) over nan/inf/-inf in responses/outputs/report; catalog join surfaces source
331	  form/membership kind/polarity/owner/display predicate by `constraint_id`; every result carries
332	  `executable_fingerprint` (INV-5); `IncompatibleStore` → new-lineage message (not a traceback).
333	- **Suite green + Ruff clean** (spec success criterion).
334	
335	## Next-Stage Handoff
336	
337	- **Fixed** (do not relitigate): CLI Option A declarative config (orchestrator D-CLI); tracking-key
338	  scoped to surfacing the fingerprint boundary (D-track); `[HARD]` non-mutation, evidence-preserving
339	  `assessment_failed`, sentinel decode, resume-refuses-changed-fingerprint, three-states-×-three-
340	  verdicts; `decode_evidence` lives beside `encode_evidence` (D5); policy closes over config, runner
341	  call site untouched (D3).
342	- **Open (plan decides mechanism):** exact `ObjectiveSpec`/`response_roles` field shapes and the
343	  penalty-threshold config; the console-script name (`teax-study` proposed); `inspect` output
344	  rendering (table vs. JSON lines).
345	- **De-risk first:** INV-4, the create→run→crash→resume→query round-trip. It exercises the config
346	  round-trip (B1), the crash seam (D8), and the query join in one test. Build the config schema +
347	  the semantic fingerprint (D2) before anything else, then stand up the end-to-end skeleton against
348	  the real evaluator so the resume-identity property is proven early.
349	- **Low-stakes / droppable:** budget/retention interpretation (D9) — not load-bearing for
350	  acceptance; ship if cheap, defer if it fights the schedule.
351	
352	---
353	
354	**Next Step:** After approval → `/_my_plan`. No `design_review` warranted — the surfaces are forced
355	by the certified seams and the spec's `[HARD]` items; the only judgment calls (disposition mapping,
356	budget/retention) are low-stakes and reversible.
